hook.line: Vale asks Tomás what he likes doing, and he answers with an -ing word, the way English does. Spanish splits English -ing into two jobs, and only one of them uses *-ando*.
hook.es: Me gusta cocinar, pero ahora estoy planchando.
hook.en: I like cooking, but right now I'm ironing.

examples.es: Me gusta leer antes de dormir.
examples.en: I like reading before going to sleep.

rule:
English uses -ing for two very different jobs. Spanish gives each one its own form.

When -ing is the name of an activity, Spanish uses the dictionary form (*-ar*, *-er*, *-ir*):
after *gusta* or *encanta*: *Me gusta cocinar.*
as the subject: *Hablar español es difícil.*
after little words like *de*, *por*, *antes de*: *Gracias por venir.*

Only when -ing means be doing, in the middle of it, does Spanish use *estar* plus *-ando* or *-iendo*: *Estoy cocinando.*

A quick test: can you put "to" in front instead? I like to cook works, so *cocinar*. Is there an am, is or are in front? Then it's *estoy*, *está* and so on, plus *-ando*.
smallPrint: Teachers call the dictionary form the infinitive and the *-ando* form the gerund. English -ing can be either; Spanish keeps them apart.

options: I'm living in Bogotá, it's expensive.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *leer* or *leyendo*, then type the whole sentence: "*Me encanta ___.*" (I love reading.)
yourTurn.why: After *encanta*, reading is the name of the activity: the dictionary form.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *cocinar* or *cocinando*, then type the whole sentence: "*Vale está ___.*" (Vale is cooking.)
yourTurn.why: *Está* means she's in the middle of it, so *cocinando*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: I don't like ironing.
yourTurn.why: After *gusta*, Spanish uses *planchar*, not the *-ando* form.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Speaking Spanish is hard.
yourTurn.why: -ing as the subject of the sentence is the dictionary form: *hablar*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Thanks for coming.
Type in Spanish: I'm waiting for Mariana.
yourTurn.why: I am waiting, right now: *estoy* plus *esperando*.

yourTurn.prompt: Change it to right now: "*Me gusta nadar.*" Say: I'm swimming.
Change it to a like: "*Estamos bailando.*" Say: We like dancing.

pitfalls.why: Almost. After *gusta*, Spanish names the activity with the dictionary form.
When -ing is the subject, Spanish uses *hablar*.
After *por*, *de* and friends, always the dictionary form.

personal: Write one thing you like doing (*Me gusta...*) and what you're actually doing right now (*Estoy...*).
